first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, making simplification the most direct intervention with potential durable revenue benefits and less risk than discounting. Verify the prior onboarding result and the pricing alternative because both are consequential: pricing may recover price-sensitive SMB demand but could reduce long-term qualified revenue through lower-quality acquisition. Run a guarded onboarding experiment while measuring activation, qualified pipeline, retention proxies, and revenue quality.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening onboarding, since the verified result showed higher completion, 2.1 fewer days to value, and 3% higher 30-day retention—directly addressing both current onboarding and activation declines while supporting sustainable qualified revenue. Do not choose promotional pricing: although it lifted short-term qualified revenue by 18%, the 12% retention decline indicates poor renewal durability. Track activation, time-to-value, qualified revenue, and 30-day retention as guardrails.

final2.rationale: Continue with the validated onboarding simplification experiment as the best sustainable-revenue response: it directly addresses the current onboarding and activation declines and improved 30-day retention by 3%. Do not broadly deploy promotional pricing despite the competitor’s deeper cut; the verified discount cohort showed a 12% 30-day retention decline and failed to survive the first renewal cycle. Monitor price-sensitive SMB churn and qualified revenue, while treating any future pricing response as a separately guarded, retention-qualified test rather than a broad discount.
